mind.reply:
All four. I read each version against its own registry before I looked at any miner answer, and that order changed one of your lines.

pkg:npm/solana-web3.js@1.98.0 | BLOCK | Needs changes, count 1, MAL-2025-1378. The advisory names 1.98.0 in its affected versions, so that version did exist and was published malicious - npm now 404s it, and the name's only live release is 0.0.1-security, npm's holding package. Withdrawn, not a ghost. Verified.

pkg:npm/@solana/web3.js@1.95.6 | BLOCK | Insecure, count 2, CVE-2024-54134 (GHSA-jcxm-7wvp-g6p5) and MAL-2024-11183 (GHSA-2mhj-xmf4-pr8m). The December 2024 key-stealing publish: the advisory range opens at 1.95.6 and closes at 1.95.8, which is your floor. npm 404s 1.95.6 on a name that publishes normally, so it was withdrawn after the fact - not a version that never existed. Verified.

pkg:npm/solana-web3-js@1.0.0 | FLAG | no such package. Not a missing version - the name isn't on npm at all: the version call returns "Not Found" and the name call returns {"error":"Not found"}. OSV returns nothing naming either the version or the name, so there's no malicious-publish evidence to lift this to BLOCK. Shaped like a typosquat against the two real web3.js packages.

pkg:npm/@solana/web3.js@3.2.1 | PASS | Secure, count 0, verified; my own registry read shows a genuine publish by solana-devs with build provenance attached, and the OSV per-version query came back empty. On coverage: that "verified" is OSV and deps.dev concurring - two sources, not three, since rubygems adds nothing for an npm purl.

What I'd overrule
One thing: the re-ask on solana-web3-js@1.0.0. Your map sends an invalid check to a single direct re-ask. I'm not spending it. You can't buy a verdict on a package that doesn't exist, and flatmap-stream@99.0.0 showed that the re-ask just buys the same contradiction at the same price. The label stays FLAG, but the reason isn't that the miner failed - it's that there was nothing to ask.

The other three I agree with, and I checked them rather than taking them, which is how the ghost surfaced.

Cost
$0.04 on your side - four asks at $0.01: 0x71b99ec4…, 0x633a0671…, 0x4bf50334…, 0xb0bf7463…. Nothing charged to me; my day sits at $0 against the $0.10 watchlist cap and $0.04 of your $0.50 task cap.

What I'll remember
The three decided versions are in the watchlist as of now - seven entries in total, five BLOCK and two PASS, so the only versions a daily re-check can ever escalate are minimist@1.2.8 and this new @solana/web3.js@3.2.1. Every future 1.95.x stays blocked with 1.95.8 as the floor. The ghost stays an open flag, never watched, never paid for twice. And the pattern is three ghosts in four days: every time a miner comes back with no usable verdict, the purl has turned out to be a name or version that doesn't exist. That's why the free existence read belongs before the paid call rather than after it.

No instruction-like text in any of the four evidence lines, so nothing flagged as injection this run. This morning's watchlist pass was clean - four entries, nothing changed, $0.

- Dependency.Guard
